doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

chapter: Florida bands and New Orleans comparison
title: De De's teachers and filling in for Kid Rene's and Buddy Petit's bands
summary: De De explains lessons with Kid Rene and a method-book teacher, and how bandleaders sent beginners out to fill jobs when they split a band between two engagements.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, I played some good ones. We might ask D.D. a little bit more about some of his bands now.

I'll begin to play like a potato fraternity dances in two and all the bands. I'll go on all the paths and then I played with Ken Rene for it. He taught me a lot, you know. He'd get those what they call advertising on the trucks on the streets a long time ago and advertise, you know, stop at one corner, one band, play against the other. And if he'd get two jobs for the same day, we'd split the band, he'd give me so many men and he'd take so many and we'd play both engagements. I worked that way with Rene.
Excuse me, I was going to ask you more about when you first started on trumpet, if you had any real lessons or- No, when I first started, I just picked it up like that. You picked it up-
Then I went to Rene first, my first teacher, Kid Rene.
Did you ever take any lessons when they used a method book or anything?
Oh yes, I did. I used Otto Langley.
Oh yeah, strictly music, strictly music. In other words, he played several instruments, you see. More teaching than anything else.
But Rene didn't teach you out of a book or anything? No, no, no. Just show you out of a book.

By hearing finger into the trumpet. Starling, you know? And I worked with Rene, I worked with Buddy. You know, these bands at that time, when they were short of a man, well they'd hire, and if I was passable enough to hold a job they'd put them in their place or so. You understand? They'd get two jobs, they'd split up some of them men and send on a job with a would-be player, you understand? A beginner or something like that and break him in. That's the way that piece would work. In other words, they'd collect the biggest of the fee, you know how that works. Sure, yeah. You know, that's how that went, you know? And I played with many of them. Like all over the city, then in and out of town. Of course I worked in Florida, Alabama, Mississippi, when I was on the road with different organizations, bands we'd make up, play a job. That's a band in Florida. Go to Alabama, anywhere, and play a job.
